newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bank Melbourne soars on Westpac offer.
newsitem.headline: Bank Melbourne soars on Westpac offer.

text.p: Shares in takeover target Bank of Melbourne Ltd soared over 10 percent when its shares resumed trading on Thursday following the announced proposed merger with Westpac Banking Corp.
At 11.15 a.m. (0115 GMT), Bank of Melbourne shares had eased back to be 62 cents higher at A$9.42 with just over 414,403 shares traded. The shares briefly touched the A$9.75 offer price from Westpac.
At the same time, Westpac shares were 4.3 cents lower at A$6.83 on light volume, off an earlier low of A$6.77. The Westpac offer values the Victorian based bank at A$1.435 billion.
"The initial response on the Westpac-Bank of Melbourne deal is that the price they are paying is probably too low," HSBC James Capel institutional advisor David Irons told Reuters.

Irons said the offer was worth about A$10.20 per share once the dividend franking elements was taken into account, but this was no good to foreign shareholders, who are not given franking on dividends.
"It would probably lead to a bit of arbitraging from locals buying from the overseas groups to try and pass on the benefit that way," Irons said.
Bank of Melbourne preference shares also rose strongly. By 11.20 a.m. (0120 GMT), they were up 50 cents or 3.40 percent at A$15.20.
